## Project Overview

This notebook prepares **CYBHI EBP/CDEP** Pre-School Outcome Questionnaire (P-OQ) assessment data for analysis and reporting (SQ 3.13, overall distress, alongside the Y-OQ). It ingests the raw eInsight export, checks and converts item values, computes total scores, pairs initial and follow-up assessments, and computes the Reliable Change Index (RCI), mirroring the YOQ script.

**Data source:** `P-OQ.csv` (file name set in Setup) — eInsight Individual Assessments export, caregiver-completed. Assumed to use the same single-row header as the Y-OQ export (`janitor::clean_names()` is sufficient; item columns start with `x`).

**Scoring** follows the *P-OQ Administration and Scoring Manual*:

-   35 items answered Never / Sometimes / Often / Almost always.
-   The 28 problem items score 1, 2, 3, 4. The 7 positive items (1, 2, 12, 21, 25, 26, 35) score 2, 1, −1, −2. Total = sum of the item scores, range 14–126. Higher scores indicate more distress.
-   The form prints these scores under each answer, so the export is assumed to hold them (`poq_export_has_form_scores <- TRUE` in Setup). If it holds answer positions (1–4 for every item) instead, set it to `FALSE` and the positive items are converted. The read stops if the positive items contradict the setting (scores 3 or 4 when form scores are expected, or negative values when positions are expected).
-   Values outside the form's scores are set to `NA` and counted.
-   **Missing items (published rule):** with one or two blank items, each takes the mean of the answered items, rounded to the nearest whole number. With 3 or more blank the total is `NA`. (The manual treats more than 10% blank, 4 or more, as uninterpretable and describes filling in only one or two, so 3 blank is also `NA`.)
-   **RCI = initial score − follow-up score.** The manual's reliable change value is 7 points: RCI ≥ 7 = "reliably better"; RCI ≤ −7 = "reliably worse"; `meaningful_change` = either.
-   The manual's clinical cutoff (47) is not applied here, as for the Y-OQ.

**Pairing logic:** Clients are grouped by `client_system_id`. The first assessment is the initial; the last assessment (if ≥2 exist) is the follow-up. Clients with only one assessment are excluded. No minimum gap is enforced; `days_since_initial` is included so a gap rule can be applied downstream.

**Output:**

| File | Contents |
|------|----------|
| `poq_paired_clean.csv` | One row per client: initial/follow-up scores, `rci`, `reliably_better`, `reliably_worse`, `meaningful_change`, quarter labels, `days_since_initial` (same columns as the YOQ outputs) |

# Setup

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)

# ---- Configuration: edit paths and reporting window here ----
in_dir  <- "/Users/cristin/CWS Dropbox/Cristin Young/CYBHI Project/Data/eInsight Exports/Individual Assessments"
out_dir <- "/Users/cristin/CWS Dropbox/Cristin Young/CYBHI Project/Rebecca and Tristan and Cristin/EInsight Data"

start_date <- as.Date("2024-01-01")
end_date   <- as.Date("2027-03-31")   # final-report data window (D1); filters nothing on interim exports

poq_file <- "P-OQ.csv"

# TRUE if item values are the scores printed on the form (positive items 2, 1,
# -1, -2); FALSE if they are answer positions 1-4 for every item.
poq_export_has_form_scores <- TRUE
```

# Helper Functions

```{r helpers}
# ---- Shared helpers (identical across the cleaning scripts) ----

# Parses eInsight date strings in ISO (2024-03-15) or US (03/15/2024) format,
# with or without a time stamp. Warns with a count of non-blank values that
# could not be parsed (these become NA and are dropped by the date filter).
parse_einsight_date <- function(x, label = "date_completed") {
  x   <- na_if(str_squish(as.character(x)), "")
  out <- as.Date(parse_date_time(
    x,
    orders = c("Ymd", "mdY", "mdy", "Ymd HMS", "Ymd HM", "mdY HMS", "mdY HM"),
    quiet  = TRUE
  ))
  n_bad <- sum(!is.na(x) & is.na(out))
  if (n_bad > 0) {
    warning(label, ": ", n_bad, " non-blank value(s) could not be parsed as dates and were set to NA.",
            call. = FALSE)
  }
  out
}

# Removes demo/test rows (provider_id or client_system_id contains "DEMO") and
# rows with no client_system_id (they cannot be linked or paired). Rows with a
# missing provider_id are kept. Prints a count for each.
remove_demo_rows <- function(df, label) {
  missing_ids <- setdiff(c("provider_id", "client_system_id"), names(df))
  if (length(missing_ids) > 0) {
    stop(label, ": column(s) needed for the demo filter not found: ",
         paste(missing_ids, collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE)
  }
  is_demo   <- coalesce(str_detect(df$provider_id, "DEMO"), FALSE) |
               coalesce(str_detect(df$client_system_id, "DEMO"), FALSE)
  no_client <- is.na(df$client_system_id) & !is_demo
  cat(label, "- rows read:", nrow(df),
      "| DEMO rows removed:", sum(is_demo),
      "| rows with no client_system_id removed:", sum(no_client),
      "| rows with missing provider_id (kept):", sum(is.na(df$provider_id) & !is_demo & !no_client), "\n")
  df[!is_demo & !no_client, ]
}

# Stops if the number of item columns differs from what scoring expects.
# Scoring is positional, so a missing or extra column would silently shift
# reverse-scored items and weights onto the wrong questions.
check_items <- function(cols, expected, label) {
  if (length(cols) != expected) {
    stop(label, ": expected ", expected, " item columns but found ", length(cols), ":\n  ",
         paste(cols, collapse = "\n  "), call. = FALSE)
  }
  message(label, ": found ", expected, " item columns as expected.")
  invisible(cols)
}

# Converts item columns to numeric. Values that are non-numeric or outside
# [min, max] are set to NA and counted (e.g., a stray "9" or text in a score column).
clean_item_scores <- function(df, cols, min, max, label) {
  num   <- df[cols] |> mutate(across(everything(), ~ suppressWarnings(as.numeric(.x))))
  raw_m <- as.matrix(df[cols])
  num_m <- as.matrix(num)
  n_non_numeric  <- sum(!is.na(raw_m) & is.na(num_m))
  n_out_of_range <- sum(num_m < min | num_m > max, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (n_non_numeric + n_out_of_range > 0) {
    warning(label, ": ", n_non_numeric, " non-numeric and ", n_out_of_range,
            " out-of-range (", min, "-", max, ") item value(s) set to NA.", call. = FALSE)
  } else {
    message(label, ": all item values are numeric and within ", min, "-", max, ".")
  }
  df[cols] <- num |> mutate(across(everything(), ~ if_else(.x < min | .x > max, NA_real_, .x)))
  df
}

# After reverse scoring, every item should correlate positively with the sum of
# the anchor items (excluding itself). Pass the items the instrument never
# reverse-scores as `anchor`: comparing against all items can hide a block of
# reversed items that mostly agree with each other. A negative value means the
# item's direction is wrong (reversed twice, or a positively worded item that
# was not reversed). Returns only the items that need a look (empty = all fine).
item_rest_check <- function(df, cols, label, anchor = cols) {
  anchor_sum <- rowSums(df[anchor], na.rm = TRUE)
  out <- tibble(
    item        = cols,
    item_rest_r = map_dbl(cols, function(col) {
      rest <- anchor_sum - if (col %in% anchor) coalesce(df[[col]], 0) else 0
      suppressWarnings(cor(df[[col]], rest, use = "pairwise.complete.obs"))
    })
  )
  n_neg <- sum(out$item_rest_r < 0, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (n_neg > 0) {
    warning(label, ": ", n_neg, " item(s) correlate negatively with the rest of the scale; ",
            "check reverse scoring (see table).", call. = FALSE)
  } else {
    message(label, ": all item-rest correlations are positive.")
  }
  out |> filter(item_rest_r < 0 | is.na(item_rest_r))
}

# Missing-item policy (decided October 2026, D10): use the instrument's
# published rule where one exists; otherwise allow up to 10% of items to be
# blank and prorate. Filled-in values are rounded half up to whole numbers,
# as the published rules do.
round_half_up <- function(x) floor(x + 0.5)

default_max_missing <- function(n_items) floor(0.10 * n_items)

# Scores a total from a data frame holding only the item columns. Rows with
# more than `max_missing` blank items get NA. Otherwise blanks are filled in
# by `method`:
#   "prorate":   total = sum of answered items x number of items / number answered
#   "item_mean": each blank item takes the rounded mean of the answered items
#   "zero":      blank items count as 0 (the PSC-35 rule)
# When `label` is given, reports how many totals were filled in or set to NA.
score_total <- function(items, max_missing, method = c("prorate", "item_mean", "zero"), label = NULL) {
  method   <- match.arg(method)
  items    <- as.matrix(items)
  answered <- rowSums(!is.na(items))
  n_blank  <- ncol(items) - answered
  item_sum <- rowSums(items, na.rm = TRUE)
  total <- switch(method,
    prorate   = round_half_up(item_sum * ncol(items) / answered),
    item_mean = item_sum + n_blank * round_half_up(item_sum / answered),
    zero      = item_sum
  )
  total[n_blank > max_missing] <- NA_real_
  if (!is.null(label)) {
    message(label, ": ", sum(n_blank > 0 & n_blank <= max_missing), " total(s) with up to ",
            max_missing, " blank item(s) filled in (", method, "); ", sum(n_blank > max_missing),
            " set to NA (more than ", max_missing, " of ", ncol(items), " items blank).")
  }
  total
}
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 1. Read and Score

```{r poq-read}
poq_raw <- read_csv(file.path(in_dir, poq_file), na = c("-", "", "NA", "N/A"), show_col_types = FALSE,
                    col_types = cols(.default = "c")) |>
  janitor::clean_names() |>
  remove_demo_rows("P-OQ")

item_cols <- names(poq_raw)[startsWith(names(poq_raw), "x")]
check_items(item_cols, 35, "P-OQ")

# Published scoring constants
poq_positive_items  <- c(1, 2, 12, 21, 25, 26, 35)
poq_positive_scores <- c(2, 1, -1, -2)   # Never, Sometimes, Often, Almost always
poq_max_missing     <- 2                 # fill in 1-2 blank items; more = NA
poq_rci             <- 7

pos_cols <- item_cols[poq_positive_items]
neg_cols <- setdiff(item_cols, pos_cols)

# The positive items show which coding the export uses: form scores include
# negative values, answer positions include 3 and 4
pos_raw    <- unlist(poq_raw[pos_cols], use.names = FALSE)
pos_values <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(pos_raw))
looks_like_positions <- any(pos_values %in% 3:4) && !any(pos_values < 0, na.rm = TRUE)
if (looks_like_positions == poq_export_has_form_scores) {
  stop("P-OQ: the positive items look like ", if (looks_like_positions) "answer positions" else "form scores",
       ", but poq_export_has_form_scores is ", poq_export_has_form_scores, ". Values found: ",
       paste(sort(unique(pos_values)), collapse = ", "), ". Update the setting in Setup.", call. = FALSE)
}

# Positive items: keep only the form's scores (converting positions if needed)
pos_codes <- if (poq_export_has_form_scores) poq_positive_scores else 1:4
n_bad_pos <- sum(!is.na(pos_raw) & !pos_values %in% pos_codes)
if (n_bad_pos > 0) {
  warning("P-OQ: ", n_bad_pos, " positive-item value(s) are not on the form's scale and were set to NA.",
          call. = FALSE)
}

poq_items <- poq_raw |>
  clean_item_scores(neg_cols, min = 1, max = 4, label = "P-OQ problem items") |>
  mutate(across(all_of(pos_cols), ~ poq_positive_scores[match(as.numeric(.x), pos_codes)]))

poq_scores <- poq_items |>
  mutate(date_completed = parse_einsight_date(date_completed)) |>
  filter(between(date_completed, start_date, end_date)) |>
  mutate(
    # P-OQ manual: 1-2 blank items take the rounded mean of the answered items
    total_score = score_total(pick(all_of(item_cols)), poq_max_missing, method = "item_mean", label = "P-OQ")
  ) |>
  select(client_system_id, collection, date_completed, total_score)

cat("P-OQ rows after scoring:  ", nrow(poq_scores), "\n")
cat("P-OQ missing total_score: ", sum(is.na(poq_scores$total_score)), "\n")
```

Direction check after scoring (higher should mean more distress on every item, including the positive items; an empty table means all correlate positively with the problem items):

```{r poq-direction}
item_rest_check(poq_items, item_cols, "P-OQ", anchor = neg_cols)
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 2. Pair Initial and Follow-up

```{r poq-pair}
poq_paired <- poq_scores |>
  group_by(client_system_id) |>
  arrange(date_completed, .by_group = TRUE) |>
  summarise(
    n_assessments   = n(),
    initial_date    = first(date_completed),
    initial_score   = first(total_score),
    follow_up_date  = if_else(n_assessments >= 2, last(date_completed), as.Date(NA)),
    follow_up_score = if_else(n_assessments >= 2, last(total_score),    NA_real_),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(follow_up_date)) |>
  mutate(
    # RCI = baseline − follow-up; positive = doing better (lower distress)
    rci                = initial_score - follow_up_score,
    reliably_better    = rci >= poq_rci,
    reliably_worse     = rci <= -poq_rci,
    meaningful_change  = reliably_better | reliably_worse,
    initial_quarter    = paste0("Q", quarter(initial_date),    " ", year(initial_date)),
    follow_up_quarter  = paste0("Q", quarter(follow_up_date), " ", year(follow_up_date)),
    days_since_initial = as.integer(follow_up_date - initial_date)
  )

cat("P-OQ paired clients:", nrow(poq_paired), "\n")
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 3. Quick Check

```{r poq-check}
# Percentages use all pairs with a valid RCI as the denominator.
poq_paired |>
  summarise(
    n_pairs                   = n(),
    n_missing_rci             = sum(is.na(rci)),
    n_valid                   = sum(!is.na(rci)),
    n_reliably_better         = sum(reliably_better, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_reliably_worse          = sum(reliably_worse,  na.rm = TRUE),
    n_no_reliable_change      = sum(!meaningful_change, na.rm = TRUE),
    pct_reliably_better       = round(100 * n_reliably_better / n_valid, 1),
    pct_reliably_worse        = round(100 * n_reliably_worse  / n_valid, 1),
    pct_no_reliable_change    = round(100 * n_no_reliable_change / n_valid, 1),
    pct_better_among_changers = round(100 * n_reliably_better /
                                        (n_reliably_better + n_reliably_worse), 1),
    n_fu_within_3_days        = sum(days_since_initial <= 3, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
```

# 4. Write Clean CSV

```{r write-csv}
write_csv(poq_paired, file.path(out_dir, "poq_paired_clean.csv"))

cat("CSV written successfully.\n")
```
